questions.question: Explain, using a pattern, why (−1) × (−4) must equal 4.
questions.expected_answer: 3 × (−4) = −12, 2 × (−4) = −8, 1 × (−4) = −4, 0 × (−4) = 0; each time the first factor drops by one the product rises by 4, so (−1) × (−4) = 4.

questions.question: What is the sign of a product of seven negative integers, and why?
questions.expected_answer: Negative. Each pair of negative factors gives a positive, so an even count of negatives is positive and an odd count is negative; seven is odd.

questions.question: Evaluate −3 × (2 − 7) + 12 ÷ (−4), showing the order of operations.
questions.expected_answer: Brackets: 2 − 7 = −5. Multiply and divide: −3 × (−5) = 15 and 12 ÷ (−4) = −3. Add: 15 + (−3) = 12.
